messages:
kira: Heads up — paging this thread because we saw a quiet spike in cross-region dispatches from EU customers to US aux last 20m. Not a full outage but a loop-ish pattern where requests get retried and hit fallbacks repeatedly. Anyone seeing it on console?

sam: I have the traces open. Looks like for certain gold-tier customers the routing policy tried primary eu-west, then aux-us and then re-evaluated and sent back to eu-west on a soft-retry (policy TTL mismatch?). small logs: `route_decision: PRIMARY->AUX->PRIMARY` repeated 3x for same request id.

nathan: ops-bot showed a surge: `redispatch_count` climbing from 0.02% to 2.1% of requests. No capacity alarms. This started ~2005001000.

ops-bot: Incident alert: cluster-routing anomalies detected for shard eu-w*. Metric: redispatch_loop_rate > 0.5% for 5m. Link: https://console.redwood/alerts/9876

ryan: My hunch — a recent rollout of the tiered-policy patch (rollout 202) added an optimization that revalidates variant-compat at decision time. If the compatibility cache is stale, policy picks aux and then background refresh flips primary back in. That could cause a bounce.

lex: Can you paste the policy snippet (the new one)? I want to check TTL/priority weighting.

sam: snippet from prod routing policy (redacted):
```
route_policies:
  - id: tiered-eu-gold
    priority: [PRIMARY, AUX]
    checks:
      - kv_cache_compat(ttl=30s)
      - quota_gate
    on_mismatch: redispatch
```
seems `kv_cache_compat` TTL is 30s — but our background validator runs every 10s and might flip values asynchronously.

kira: So flow is: request -> primary selected because cache says ok -> background validation fails -> on_mismatch triggers redispatch -> aux selected -> background validation re-runs and marks primary ok -> another redispatch back. Repeat.

nathan: Confirmed in trace: `on_mismatch` fires even when mismatch is transient; there's no backoff or circuit breaker on redispatch. That explains rapid back-and-forth.

ryan: Quick mitigation: patch `on_mismatch` to prefer failover-with-hold for N seconds instead of immediate redispatch, or add an exponential backoff on redispatch per-request. Thoughts?

lex: For emergency hotfix I'd prefer changing behavior to `on_mismatch: fallback_hold(60s)` which pins the chosen aux for that request group for 60s. Less invasive than changing cache TTLs.

sam: Agreed. We can ship a hotfix to routing config (config rollout, not code) and monitor redispatch_rate. I can prepare the config with a 30s hold.

kira: Do we need a rollback path? If aux has a bug, holding could route bad responses for longer. We should gate this to gold-tier only for the hotfix.

ryan: Good call. Use targeted policy: `tiered-eu-gold` only. Add telemetry flag `redispatch_hold_active: true` to easily revoke.

nathan: I'll add a temporary SLO to watch response correctness: `error_rate.gold.tiered_eu` and increase retention for related logs.

ops-bot: Deploy plan issued by kira: config-change -> progressive rollout 10% -> 100% in 10m -> monitor redispatch_rate and error_rate. Approvals: @ops @infra required.

sam: Pushed config PR: `config#1248` with `fallback_hold: 30s` targeted at tiered-eu-gold. Patchset includes telemetry tag.

ryan: Quick verification on staging matched expected behavior (no bounce). sample traces: `PRIMARY->HOLDED_AUX` then finish.

kira: Ops, can you approve the rollout? If we see aux error spike we revert the flag.

nathan: Approved from SRE side. Also created alert: `redispatch_hold_error_rate > 0.2%` to trigger rollback.

ops-bot: Approval recorded. Rolling out `config#1248` to prod canary (10% of gold) at 2005001160.

sam: Canary metrics at +3m: redispatch_rate for canary customers down from 1.8% to 0.05%. No error spike.

kira: Good. Continue rollout, watch latency and token cost. Add a postmortem note: investigate why `kv_cache_compat` validator is flipping values intermittently — maybe race or incorrect TTL semantics.

ryan: Follow-ups (assigned): lex to add unit + integration test for transient compatibility flips; nathan to increase cache instrumentation to record change source; sam to add dashboard tile showing redispatch_count per-tier and per-region; kira to write outage blameless writeup if needed.

lex: I'll also propose a PR to make `on_mismatch` semantics explicit in the routing-engine docs so future rollouts don't surprise.

kira: tl;dr — hotfix config rolled (hold=30s for gold EU), immediate reduction in redispatch loops, monitoring added, next steps: root-cause on validator flips + test coverage + docs. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
